items.title: Bitget Exchange Suffers $387.5M Hack
points: Attackers accessed Bitget's backend wallet infrastructure and spoofed (fabricated) transaction data to make unauthorized payouts appear legitimate to security systems.
CEO Grady Chen says the $464 million protection fund will cover all customer losses; withdrawals remain frozen until September 26.
North Korean attribution based on matching IP addresses and on-chain activity patterns, adding to an estimated $2.1 billion in illicit gains by such groups.
This is the largest known crypto exchange hack of 2026, surpassing prior major incidents.

items.title: Magic Eden Ethereum NFT Listing Vulnerability
points: A flaw in Limit Break's Payment Processor V2 exposed older Magic Eden Ethereum NFT listings to exploitation.
Whitehat security researchers rescued more than 23,000 NFTs before malicious actors could exploit the vulnerability.
Magic Eden alerted holders to verify older Ethereum listings for exposure and take protective action.

items.title: Institutional Growth in Prediction Markets
points: Morgan Stanley's entry into NEXTPredict signals growing institutional appetite for on-chain prediction markets (platforms letting users bet crypto on real-world event outcomes).
Current prediction market activity remains heavily weighted toward sports betting rather than broader institutional use cases.
Valuations increasingly depend on achieving higher levels of institutional participation to justify market multiples.

items.title: SEC Guidance on Crypto Securities Classification
points: The SEC issued updated guidance clarifying the legal status of crypto assets under securities laws.
New rules distinguish utility tokens (digital assets providing access to a service) from security tokens (assets representing ownership or investment contracts).
Bitcoin rebounded above $85,000 following the announcement, signaling market confidence in clearer rules.
Guidance is expected to reduce regulatory uncertainty for crypto projects and investors going forward.

headlines: Bitget crypto exchange loses $387.5 million in hack—likely 2026's largest—with attackers spoofing backend wallet transactions to bypass authorization processes.
CEO Grady Chen attributes attack to North Korean hackers based on IP addresses and on-chain patterns, adding to estimated $2.1 billion in illicit gains by such groups.
Customer balances remain protected via a $464 million insurance fund, though withdrawals are frozen until September 26.
Magic Eden NFT platform alerts users that older Ethereum listings face exposure from a Limit Break Payment Processor flaw; 23,000+ NFTs rescued via whitehat effort.
Morgan Stanley joins prediction markets platform NEXTPredict as institutional interest in on-chain betting grows beyond sports wagering.

sections.title: Bitget Exchange Suffers $387.5M Hack
points: 1. Attackers accessed Bitget's backend wallet infrastructure and spoofed (fabricated) transaction data to make unauthorized payouts appear legitimate to the exchange's own security systems.
2. CEO Chen says $464 million protection fund will cover all customer losses, ensuring account balances remain unaffected despite frozen withdrawals during investigation.

3. North Korean attribution based on matching IP addresses and on-chain activity patterns consistent with known state-sponsored hacking groups; would represent latest loss in documented $2.1B theft tally by such actors.
4. Represents the largest known crypto exchange hack of 2026, surpassing prior major incidents in scale and impact.

sections.title: Magic Eden Ethereum NFT Listing Vulnerability
points: 1. Flaw in Limit Break's Payment Processor V2 exposed old Magic Eden Ethereum NFT listings to exploitation by attackers.
2. Whitehat security researchers rescued more than 23,000 NFTs before malicious actors could exploit the vulnerability.
3. Alerts issued to NFT holders to verify their older Ethereum listings for potential exposure and take protective action.

sections.title: Institutional Growth in Prediction Markets
points: 1. Morgan Stanley's entry into NEXTPredict signals growing institutional appetite for on-chain prediction markets (platforms allowing users to bet on real-world event outcomes and stake crypto on predictions).
2. Current prediction market activity remains heavily weighted toward sports betting rather than broader institutional use cases.
3. Valuations increasingly dependent on achieving higher levels of institutional participation to justify market multiples.

headlines: SEC releases new guidance clarifying which crypto assets qualify as securities, providing regulatory clarity for the industry.
Bitcoin rebounds above $85,000 amid the regulatory announcement, signaling market confidence in clearer rules.
New framework aims to distinguish between utility tokens and security tokens based on how they function and how funds are used.

sections.title: SEC Guidance on Crypto Securities Classification
points: 1. The SEC issued updated guidance to clarify the legal status of crypto assets under securities laws.
2. The distinction between utility tokens (digital assets providing access to a service) and security tokens (assets representing ownership or investment contracts) forms the basis of the new rules.
3. Guidance is expected to reduce regulatory uncertainty for crypto projects and investors going forward.
